Collecting is the Trustee's job, valuing is the Assessor's, and the County Commission sets the rate. Both offices are on Public Square in Columbia and keep weekday hours from eight to four.

  • Trustee: One Public Square, Columbia, TN 38401, 931-375-2201. Make checks out to Maury County Trustee and mail them to that address.
  • Assessor of Property: 6 Public Square, Columbia, TN 38401, 931-375-4001.
  • Rate: voted each year by the Maury County Commission.

Bills go to whoever held title on New Year's Day, and a change of mailing address is reported to the Assessor. The Trustee's page covers both points. If your house is in Columbia, Spring Hill or Mount Pleasant, ask city hall whether a separate city bill applies.

Maury County lies south of Nashville and has grown fast. Columbia holds the courthouse, and Spring Hill, which straddles the Williamson County line, is the largest city. The county counted 118,131 people on July 1, 2025, up 17.0% from April 2020, and has 49,725 housing units, 70.9% of them owner-occupied. The typical owner-occupied house is valued at $355,700, rent in the middle is $1,300 and household income in the middle is $76,130. Builders took out 1,408 permits in 2025.

Interstate 65, State Route 396 and US 31 tie the county to Nashville, which explains much of the demand. Maury County Public Schools runs the public schools countywide.

This county reappraises every four years, and 2026 is a reappraisal year. The appraisal on file reflects market value as of January 1 of that year, with later improvements added at equalized value. Prices have climbed across the county, so an owner whose house was last valued before the recent run-up should read the new notice closely.

The math is short. Take the appraised value, multiply by the assessment ratio for the property's class, and apply the rate to each $100 of the result. Tennessee assesses residential property at 25 percent of appraised value.

The county's 2025 to 2026 budget letter to the state Comptroller shows a rate of $1.91 for each $100 of assessment, with no increase for residents. A reappraisal year can bring a different rate, so ask the Trustee which one is on your current bill. The Assessor's page explains the calculation and links to reappraisal guides.

Payment opens in early October and stays open through the end of February, and all property taxes are due on receipt. A penalty and interest charge of 1.5 percent starts March 1 and grows each month. Accounts still unpaid go to Chancery Court on April 1.

The Trustee takes partial payments, though interest applies on March 1 to whatever remains. A postmark counts as the payment date, except when delinquent accounts move to Chancery Court. Tennessee does not require the county to mail a notice, so a missing bill is no defense against the charges.

  • In person at One Public Square, or in the drop box outside the office (no cash)
  • By mail to Maury County Trustee, One Public Square, Columbia, TN 38401
  • Online by credit card or e-check, with a 2.5% vendor fee
  • By phone at 1-877-556-4502
  • Monthly bank debits through the county's ACH program, set up by calling 931-375-2201

sections.h2: How to contest a new value
sections.html:
The order is Assessor, then the county equalization board, then the state board. Call 931-375-4001 to learn how and when the county board takes appeals this year.

The state's appeals guide covers the later steps. A disputed assessment generally has to start at the county board or it becomes final. The state deadline is the later of August 1 or the 45th day after the county board mailed its notice, so an owner holding a late county notice should count forward from the mailing date. An administrative judge hears the case and rules within 90 days of the hearing, and court review must be sought within 60 days once the state board's order is final.

Some assessors offer an informal review that can speed a correction. It is no appeal and protects nothing later, so ask whether the Maury office offers one and still file with the county board to keep every option.

The Trustee's office helps elderly homeowners, disabled homeowners, disabled-veteran owners and the widows or widowers of a disabled veteran apply for the Tennessee Tax Relief Program under state guidelines. Call 931-375-2201 for the forms and the current income limits.

The ACH program can also spread the bill into equal monthly bank debits. Call the same number to ask how to enroll. Spreading payments helps an owner avoid a large bill in February, but each month's debit must still clear before the March 1 charge starts.

The tax year follows the calendar, and the notice goes to whoever owned the house on January 1. A fall sale therefore leaves the seller's name on the bill even though the buyer carries the house into the next year. Request the Trustee's exact balance and let the title agent split it at closing.

Late sellers face a short clock, because charges start in March and the Chancery Court turnover follows in April. Any balance still open at closing comes out of the seller's net, so confirm the amount with the Trustee a week ahead.

Before listing, collect these items: the parcel's latest bill, proof of any monthly ACH debits, any relief paperwork, and the Assessor's value notice. If the house has been in a family for years, check whether older years show a balance. A cash sale can close fast, but the Trustee's payoff still has to be settled at the table.

faqs.q: Is 2026 a reappraisal year in Maury County?
faqs.a: Yes. Reappraisals run every four years, and 2026 is the current one. Values come from market prices as of January 1 of that year.

faqs.q: What rate does Maury County use?
faqs.a: The 2025 to 2026 budget letter shows $1.91 per $100 of assessed value. The Commission sets the rate, so check your current bill or call the Trustee for the figure now in force.

faqs.q: When do Maury County taxes become late?
faqs.a: On March 1. Interest of 1.5 percent a month starts then and climbs each month, and on April 1 the county turns delinquent accounts over to Chancery Court. Payment is open from the first Monday in October through February.

faqs.q: Does Maury County accept partial payments?
faqs.a: Yes, the Trustee accepts them. Interest still applies on March 1 to any balance left unpaid, so a partial payment lowers the amount that accrues interest without ending it.

faqs.q: Where do I send a new mailing address?
faqs.a: Call the Assessor at 931-375-4001. The Trustee's page directs address changes there, and a bill that never arrives does not remove penalty or interest.
